label: copy-phase input g (fed-back g) early in short sequences
explanation: Fires almost exclusively (99.9% of mass) when the token g is fed back as input during the copy phase, i.e. right after the model has output g. Never fires in the original phase or on <DEL>, and essentially never on other tokens. Activation is strongest when g is the first original token, so it is fed back at the first copy step (recall_idx 1, prev_tok <DEL>; top examples are all g ... <DEL> [g]), and it weakens for later copy positions and longer sequences: L >= 7 or t >= 10 are mostly silent (7.2+ give under 2% of mass). A repeated g in the copy phase usually fires more weakly than the first one. Bare (phase==2 & in_tok==g) has recall 0.99 but precision 0.30; adding L<=6 & t<=9 gives dev F1 0.86.

issues: The label and predicate hold up. The profile shows 0 activations in the original phase and 0 on <DEL>. Copy phase has 100% of the mass. in_tok==g has 27230 of 27419 active steps (99.9% of mass); the next token, n, has only 60.

The bare predicate phase==2 & in_tok==g gives P 0.30, R 0.99 and mass recall 0.999 on dev, matching the claim. The full predicate on test gives P 0.860, R 0.859, F1 0.859 and mass recall 0.971, reproducing the reported scores.

The strength claims hold. All top examples have the form g ... <DEL> [g], peaking at about 5.4. Mass by recall_idx is 1: 0.44, 2: 0.36, 3: 0.16, then near zero from 5 on. Mass by L falls sharply after 6 (L=7: 0.013, L=8 and L=9: 0.003 each). A repeated g fires more weakly, e.g. 'g g d <DEL> [g:0.98] [g:0.69]'.

The leftover errors are a graded falloff, not a separate class of cases. Test misses (3885 steps, 2.9% of mass) are tiny activations (0.01 to 0.07 of max) on fed-back g at t=10-11 or L=7. False positives are fed-back g at t=8-9 with L=6 that land just below threshold. Both sit at the threshold edge.

No better predicate turned up. Alternative cutoffs (t+L<=14 or 15, recall_idx<=3, L<=6 alone, mixed per-L cutoffs) all score test F1 0.83 to 0.85, at or below the original 0.859. Restricting to the first fed-back g lowers F1 to 0.80, so later g's are rightly included.
Minor caveat: the L<=6 & t<=9 cutoff is a hard line drawn across a smooth decline with L and t, so the predicate simplifies how the feature behaves. The explanation already says this.
